classification.difficultyReason: Derives general height and range formulas, then combines them with a double-angle identity to prove the projection angle.

content.prompt: A particle is projected from level ground with initial speed $V$ m/s at an angle of $\theta$ to the horizontal.

answer.worked:
At greatest height, $\dot y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}V\sin\theta-gt&=0\\t&=\frac{V\sin\theta}{g}.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $y=Vt\sin\theta-\frac12gt^2$:
$$\begin{align*}H&=V\sin\theta\cdot\frac{V\sin\theta}{g}-\frac12g\left(\frac{V\sin\theta}{g}\right)^2\\H&=\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{g}-\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\\H&=\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\text{ metres}.\end{align*}$$

The particle lands when $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}V\sin\theta\cdot t-\frac12gt^2&=0\\t\left(V\sin\theta-\frac12gt\right)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Taking the positive landing time,
$$t=\frac{2V\sin\theta}{g}.$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}R&=V\cos\theta\cdot\frac{2V\sin\theta}{g}\\R&=\frac{V^2(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)}{g}\\R&=\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{g}\text{ metres}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the horizontal range is five times the greatest height, prove that $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac45\right)$.

answer.worked:
Using $R=5H$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{V^2\sin 2\theta}{g}&=5\cdot\frac{V^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}\\2\sin\theta\cos\theta&=\frac52\sin^2\theta.\end{align*}$$
Divide both sides by $\sin\theta$, where $\sin\theta\ne0$:
$$\begin{align*}2\cos\theta&=\frac52\sin\theta\\\tan\theta&=\frac45\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac45\right).\end{align*}$$
